class="Figure-content"><figcaption class="Figure-caption"><p>El secretario de Estado Alexi Giannoulias lanzó su campaña a la alcaldía arremetiendo contra los primeros tres años de mandato del alcalde Brandon Johnson.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Candace Dane Chambers/Sun-Times</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>Ex tesorero estatal, Giannoulias empezó en la política como un compañero de baloncesto de Barack Obama. Jugó profesionalmente en Grecia, donde aprendió lecciones valiosas sobre competitividad, trabajo en equipo y cómo “rodearte de jugadores que sean mejores que tú para que puedas mejorar”, dijo.</p><p>No es de extrañar, entonces, que el expresidente de dos mandatos sea el mentor y modelo político de Giannoulias.</p><p>“Lo que hizo excepcionalmente bien y la lección que me enseñó en cada paso y para cada cargo al que aspiró, me dijo, ‘Asegúrate de rodearte de personas que sean mucho más inteligentes que tú en cada etapa del camino’. Eso se ha quedado grabado en mi cabeza”, dijo Giannoulias. “Busco a las personas más capaces y talentosas que tengan un entendimiento inherente de ese desafío en particular”.</p><p>Giannoulias, de 50 años, tiene cuatro hijas menores de 10 años. Dijo que él y su esposa lucharon con la decisión de lanzarse a una campaña agotadora por un trabajo “brutal” con poderes muy reducidos, problemas enormes y sin soluciones fáciles.</p><p>Chicago enfrenta un déficit de $90 millones a mitad de año, un hoyo presupuestario de más de $1,000 millones en 2027 y una crisis de pensiones de $36,000 millones con dos de los cuatro fondos de pensiones de empleados municipales rondando peligrosamente cerca de la bancarrota.</p><h3>Una decisión ‘realmente difícil’</h3><p>“Es realmente difícil cuando tienes cuatro niñas pequeñas a las que amas con todo tu corazón y quieres pasar tiempo con ellas. [Es] muy personal, muy duro para mí”, dijo Giannoulias.</p><p>“Pero amo esta ciudad y me importa esta ciudad, y quiero que me vean trabajando para ser parte de la solución. Por cursi e idealista que suene, quiero que miren hacia arriba y digan, ‘Una vez, cuando la Ciudad estaba en apuros, mi padre fue una de las muchas, muchas personas que hicieron lo mejor que pudieron de forma transparente y honesta para luchar por esta ciudad’”.</p><p>Con apenas $631,309 en su fondo de campaña frente a los casi $22 millones para Giannoulias, Johnson se apoya fuertemente en las redes sociales y en el poder de la investidura, junto con la cobertura mediática gratuita que ello conlleva.</p><p>Se espera que presente a Giannoulias como una repetición de Emanuel —un cautivo de las mismas personas que se verían más afectadas por el lema del atribulado alcalde de “imponer impuestos a los ricos”.</p><p>Giannoulias espera amortiguar algunos de esos ataques uniéndose a Johnson en la campaña por un impuesto del 3% sobre los ingresos anuales superiores a $1 millón.</p><p>Pero sabe que eso no detendrá las flechas políticas que vendrán hacia él.</p><p>“Soy un hombre. Puedo aguantarlo”, dijo Giannoulias.</p><p><i>Contribuyó: Violet Miller </i></p><p><i>Traducido con una herramienta de inteligencia artificial (IA) y editado por los seres humanos de </i><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz" target="_blank" ><i>La Voz Chicago</i></a></p>

entries.title: Bears Training Camp Report No. 6: Devin Bush breaks up goal line pass to Luther Burden
entries.summary: <p>Breaking down the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a>’ Tuesday <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/08/03/bears-training-camp-report-practice-no-5-rb-kyle-monangai-back-in-action" target="_blank" >training camp</a> practice:<br> </p><h3><b>What happened</b></h3><p>The pass game struggled to find its rhythm and blew a chance to end practice on a good note. In an 11-on-11 drill without tackling, the Bears took over at their own 47, down five, with 54 seconds left. The Bears committed two false starts but drove to the 22 with about three seconds to play.</p><p>Williams then threw a seam route to Luther Burden, who was hammered by linebacker Devin Bush. The ball fell incomplete at the goal line. Burden walked off slowly.</p><p>“I was going for the ball,” Bush said. “There was nothing malicious.”</p><p>Burden said the hit was "not typical" but was more disappointed by the result.</p><p>"I expect to catch every ball," he said.</p><h3><b>Fight!</b></h3><p>The first fight of camp: defensive lineman Jordan van den Berg, a sixth-round pick, tackled offensive lineman Caden Barnett after the two jawed at each other following a play. Defensive end Montez Sweat celebrated the hit.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">My favorite moment of <a href="https://x.com/hashtag/Bears?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">#Bears</a> camp today: a rookie fight! Jordan van den Berg tackled Caden Barnett after a play. <a href="https://t.co/OKgKsy7Dy1">pic.twitter.com/OKgKsy7Dy1</a></p>— Patrick Finley (@patrickfinley) <a href="https://x.com/patrickfinley/status/2084684769531699524?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">August 4, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p></p><h3><b>Who’s watching</b></h3><p>Former Saints tackle Terron Armstead, who played for Bears offensive line line coach Dan Roushar in New Orleans, and former Bears coach Dave Wannstedt chatted with general manager Ryan Poles. Fox host Curt Menefee watched practice, too.</p><h3><b>Injury report</b></h3><p>Cornerback Terell Smith missed practice after getting hurt Monday. </p><h3><b>What’s next</b></h3><p>The Bears practice entries.title: Estado de Indiana demanda a poblado por oponerse a posible centro de detención de ICE
entries.summary: <p>El fiscal general de Indiana demanda a una comunidad del noroeste del estado por oponerse a un posible centro de detención de inmigrantes.</p><p>El fiscal general republicano, Todd Rokita, firme partidario del presidente Donald Trump, presentó la demanda estatal la semana pasada contra el poblado de Merrillville.</p><p>Rokita invoca una ley estatal recién promulgada, la llamada Ley de Equidad, que impide las políticas de santuario locales, obliga la cooperación con órdenes federales de detención migratoria y sanciona a los empleadores que a sabiendas contraten a trabajadores no autorizados.</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-720000" name="module-720000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h3>La Voz Chicago WhatsApp</h3>Encuentra más noticias en nuestro canal de WhatsApp. <a class="Link" href="https://www.whatsapp.com/channel/0029Vb0XT1XCHDylm3rCs40P" target="_blank" ><b>Síguenos.</b></a></div> </div><p>“Solicitamos que Merrillville cumpliera con la ley estatal, y se negaron, optando en cambio por jugar, en efecto ayudar y encubrir, a extranjeros indocumentados delincuentes, y poniendo la evasión de la justicia por parte de los indocumentados por encima de la seguridad de los contribuyentes de toda la región”, dijo Rokita en un comunicado de prensa. “Eso es ilegal según la ley de Indiana.”</p><p>En enero, el Concejo Municipal de Merrillville aprobó una resolución oponiéndose a la conversión de grandes almacenes industriales en centros de procesamiento o detención del Servicio de Inmigración y Control de Aduanas (ICE). La municipalidad había sido mencionada en un informe publicado como posible sitio.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a Pasciak LaRiviere/Sun-Times</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>A principios de este mes, Rokita advirtió al concejo que estaba infringiendo la ley estatal y exigió que revocara su ordenanza. El concejo se opuso.</p><p>Rokita también ha advertido a otras entidades gubernamentales sobre bloquear o restringir a los agentes de ICE o las ha demandado, entre ellas, a <a class="Link" href="https://indianapublicradio.org/news/2025/11/rokita-sues-school-district-for-blocking-ice-from-schools/" target="_blank" >las Escuelas Públicas de Indianápolis</a>, al <a class="Link" href="https://events.in.gov/event/092425-attorney-general-todd-rokita-warns-blocking-sheriffs-cooperation-with-ice-would-be-illegal-fuel-indy-crime-surge?utm_campaign=widget&utm_medium=widget&utm_source=State+of+Indiana" target="_blank" >Concejo Municipal Indianápolis-Marion</a>, y al <a class="Link" href="https://events.in.gov/event/attorney-general-todd-rokita-investigates-potential-labor-trafficking-and-interference-with-federal-immigration-enforcement-in-monroe-county?utm_campaign=widget&utm_medium=widget&utm_source=State+of+Indiana" target="_blank" >Condado de Monroe</a>, donde se ubica Bloomington.</p><p>La concejal Keesha Hardaway dijo que no se siente intimidada por las amenazas de Rokita.</p><p>“Simplemente siento que esto viola nuestro derecho a la libertad de expresión consagrado en la Primera Enmienda. Representamos a 5,000 residentes cada uno, y somos su voz, y él está intentando callar las voces de la ciudad de Merrillville, y no voy a tolerarlo”, dijo Hardaway.</p><p>En un comunicado, un portavoz del Departamento de Seguridad Nacional (DHS) dijo que no tenía nuevos centros de detención que anunciar en Merrillville.</p><p>Lali Cuevas, fundadora del equipo de respuesta rápida, Northwest Indiana Community Response Team, dijo que Merrillville tiene razón al oponerse a ICE.</p><p>“La gente ya vive con miedo. Niños que no asisten a la escuela, familias que no pueden moverse libremente. Y con el centro de detención eso realmente va a generar aún más desconfianza”, dijo Cuevas. “Espero que sigan firmes, aunque, ya sabes, vengan multas. Yo sé que eso va a ser una carga para la municipalidad. Pero siento que debería ser un asunto de libertad de expresión”.</p><p>Las instalaciones de ICE en todo el país también han sido lugares donde los detenidos han denunciado maltrato y abusos, lo que ha llevado a que los demócratas en el Congreso tengan audiencias.</p><p>La semana pasada, la Unión Americana de Libertades Civiles (ACLU) de Indiana presentó demandas en nombre de un detenido en la instalación de detención de ICE en la Miami Correctional Facility, al norte de Indianápolis, apodada “Speedway Slammer”. El detenido sufrió una convulsión después de no recibir la medicación recetada en la instalación y luego fue rociado con gas pimienta por oficiales correccionales.</p><p>Según la cadena de televisión de Indianápolis, <a class="Link" href="https://www.wishtv.com/news/politics/aclu-reviews-merrillville-lawsuit/" target="_blank" >WISH</a>, ACLU está revisando la demanda presentada contra la municipalidad por Rokita por posibles violaciones de la Primera Enmienda.</p><p>El representante federal demócrata, Frank J. Mrvan, que representa el noroeste de Indiana en el Congreso y que se postula para la reelección este año, se opone a la presencia de ICE en la localidad y criticó a la administración de Trump por no consultar a los funcionarios locales, incluyendo a él mismo.</p><p>“Pido respetuosamente a la Administración que revierta cualquier decisión de convertir edificios comerciales con el propósito de detener a personas en nuestro distrito”, escribió Mrvan en un comunicado.</p><p><i>Michael Puente es reportero y presentador de WBEZ. Contáctalo en mpuente@wbez.org.</i></p><p><i>Traducido con una herramienta de inteligencia artificial (IA) y editado por los seres humanos de </i><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz" target="_blank" ><i>La Voz Chicago</i></a></p>

entries.title: Ownership of West Suburban, Weiss hospitals would change in potential settlement
entries.summary: <p>Lawyers for one of the owners of West Suburban Medical Center and Weiss Memorial Hospital are pushing to sell the hospitals for $1 to Insight Health Systems and demote the other owner and CEO into a temporary consulting position. </p><p>That change in ownership is a part of a potential settlement in the ongoing legal battle for control of the hospitals between the two owners: Resilience Healthcare CEO Manoj Prasad and the hospitals’ landlord, Rathnakar Reddy Patlola. </p><p>Patlola's attorneys filed a motion Friday asking Cook County Circuit Judge Patrick Stanton to either enforce the settlement agreement or appoint a receiver to take control of the hospital. The lawyers also accuse Prasad and his legal team of delaying the process and jeopardizing the settlement. </p><p>The potential settlement was finalized in late May, but only made public for the first time in a Friday court filing. Patlola's lawyers worked out the settlement agreement with a former lawyer for Prasad. That lawyer has since left the case, citing differences with Prasad. Prasad's new attorneys are now pushing for a new settlement agreement, according to Crain's Chicago Business.</p><p>Under the draft settlement filed Friday, Prasad would step down as CEO, something he has resisted and the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/health/2026/07/28/weiss-west-suburban-hospital-pritzker-prasad" target="_blank" >communities surrounding West Suburban and Weiss have been pleading for</a>.</p><p>He would be able to continue as a consultant for the hospitals for up to six months, earning $100,000. He would also get to keep the title to a 2022 Range Rover Sport owned by a subsidiary of Resilience, according to the potential deal.</p><p>The draft settlement states that both hospitals would be sold for $1 to Insight, which runs Insight Hospital and Medical Center — formerly Mercy Hospital — in Bronzeville. In 2021, <a class="Link" href="https://www.wbez.org/environment-public-health/2021/10/25/inside-the-fight-to-save-chicagos-historic-mercy-hospital" target="_blank" >Insight bought Mercy for $1</a> when it was about to close its doors. </p><p>Representatives for Prasad and Insight did not immediately reply to requests for comment.</p><p><i>Read the full motion here:</i> </p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" data-embed> <iframe src="https://docs.google.com/viewer?embedded=true&url=https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/e2/a4/91c38aaa4d71991089ece8e16628/proposed-west-sub-settlement.pdf"></iframe> </div> </div></div><p></p>

entries.title: Bears sign RT Darnell Wright to 4-year contract extension
entries.summary: <p>Darnell Wright <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/07/31/bears-training-camp-darnell-wright-contract-extension-here-long-time-nfl-ryan-poles" target="_blank" >wasn’t worried</a> about getting a contract extension done during training camp.</p><p>Turns out, he had little reason to. The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> and their standout right tackle agreed to a four-year extension worth $116 million, with $93 million guaranteed Tuesday, a source confirmed. The deal represents the most guaranteed money for a tackle in league history. His average salary of $29 million makes him the second-highest paid ever, behind Laremy Tunsil, per Spotrac.com.</p><p>The move crosses a major item off the Bears' offseason to-do list. Wright was entering the fourth year of his rookie contract. The team had picked up his fifth-year option for 2027 with a $19 million price tag.</p><p>Wright was inconsistent at the start of last season and dealt with a elbow injury but still was named a second-team all-pro. He finished as the 15th-ranked tackle in the NFL last year, per Pro Football Focus. ESPN ranked him fourth in pass-block win rate.</p><p>The Bears drafted Wright No. 10 overall in 2023 after trading down one spot. The Eagles moved up to tackle defensive tackle Jalen Carter, who got his own extension last week.</p><p>Bears general manager Ryan Poles said one week ago that it took two sides to work out a deal, but Wright painted a more optimistic picture Friday. </p><p>"The reason you have representatives is because you let those guys go in and they handle some of those things for you," Wright said. "My job is to play football and handle that part of it. Their job is to talk and so, I'm just trying to handle my piece and those things handle themselves."</p><p>He said he wasn't worried about getting a deal done because he planned on staying with the entries.title: Illinois State trooper accused of drugging, sexually assaulting bartender at bar he frequented in Tinley Park
entries.summary: <p>An Illinois State Police trooper charged with sexual assault allegedly drugged and assaulted a bartender last year in suburban Tinley Park.</p><p>Douglas Lee, 54, was stripped of his police powers and ordered held at Cook County jail after he was <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/08/03/illinois-state-trooper-sex-assault-tinley-park" target="_blank" >charged Friday</a>, according to court records and state police.</p><p>Lee is accused of drugging a woman while she was out with friends, taking her to a hotel and sexually assaulting her before leaving her in her car overnight.</p><p>According to Cook County prosecutors, Lee knew the woman and frequently visited the bar where she worked as a bartender. They met in 2024.</p><p>On Aug. 2, 2025, the woman stayed at the bar with friends after finishing her shift. The group later decided to walk to a nearby bar, and Lee asked to join them.</p><p>At the second bar, Lee allegedly bought the woman a seltzer and a shot. The woman told investigators the last thing she remembered after drinking them was dancing with a friend.</p><p>The woman woke up in her car around 10:45 a.m. the next day, prosecutors said. Her car was parked in the same spot where she had left it when she arrived for work the previous day. When she woke up, she noticed her pants were inside out, her bra was on the passenger seat and her shirt was tucked into the pocket of her jacket.</p><p>The woman then got out of her car and went into the bar to use the restroom. Afterward, she realized there were signs that she had engaged in sexual intercourse, but she had no recollection of it.</p><p>She called two of her friends she was with the night before. One friend said she had seen the woman and Lee dancing, prosecutors said.</p><p>The woman allegedly called Lee to ask for an explanation. He met her in the bar’s parking lot and admitted they had intercourse but claimed it was consensual, prosecutors said.</p><p>Video footage from the second bar showed Lee and the woman leaving the bar about 1:30 a.m. Other videos showed the woman getting into Lee’s car and driving off, prosecutors said.</p><p>Lee then drove to a hotel in Midlothian, where he paid for a room using his credit card and assaulted the woman, prosecutors said.</p><p>The woman petitioned for an order of protection against Lee, court records show. Lee was ordered to stay away from the woman and have no contact with her for the duration of the case.</p><p>Lee was arrested Thursday. Cook County Judge Shauna Boliker ordered Lee to remain held at a hearing Saturday.</p><p>Court records also show Lee was accused of assault in 2005 in connection with allegedly making threatening phone calls. The case was later dismissed.</p>

entries.title: Wrong-way Dan Ryan driver was trying to 'scare' woman pleading for her life, prosecutors say
entries.summary: <p>An Aurora man remains in custody Tuesday a day after prosecutors allege he drove the wrong way on the Dan Ryan Expressway to "scare" a woman who was pleading for her life moments before she died as a result of a five-vehicle crash. </p><p>Juan Ruiz-Huerta, 29, was charged with first degree murder, kidnapping, unlawful restraint and aggravated battery <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/2026/07/31/dan-ryan-crash" target="_blank" >related to the Friday evening crash</a> that left 28-year-old Victory A. Swanigan dead and another driver critically injured. </p><p>A Cook County judge ordered Ruiz-Huerta to remain in custody during a Monday hearing at the Leighton Criminal Courthouse. He is due back in court on Aug. 19. </p><p>Ruiz-Huerta had been pursuing Swanigan romantically for months and picked her up after a hair appointment he paid for when he had grown angry with her over the "status of their relationship," prosecutors said during the hearing. </p><p>Shortly after 5:30 p.m. Friday, Ruiz-Huerta drove onto Interstate 94 and passed slowing traffic and police lights north of 31st Street, where Swanigan screamed for help, prosecutors said. </p><p>Ruiz-Huerta then did a U-turn and began speeding south in the northbound lanes of I-94 while Swanigan could be heard by her friend begging him to slow down, according to prosecutors. </p><p>Swanigan told Ruiz-Huerta she had "three children that she wanted to see again" as he continued to speed, prosecutors said. </p><p>CTA surveillance video at 47th street then captured Ruiz-Huerta moving across multiple lanes at high speeds and swerving between multiple cars and trucks that were going in the proper direction before colliding head on with another car going north in the express lanes and causing Ruiz-Huerta's vehicle to flip over the concrete median and land in the local lanes, according to court documents.</p><p>Prosecutors noted that the other driver in the collision — who suffered multiple rib fractures, a laceration to his liver and a variety of other injuries — told investigators he tried to switch lanes to avoid the crash when Ruiz-Huerta changed lanes too. </p><p>A return on a search warrant executed on the black box of Ruiz-Huerta's 2013 Mazda X-5 showed he was traveling 86 mph five seconds before the crash and at the time of impact, he was traveling 78 mph with no depression on the brake and a 25% depression on the accelerator, authorities said.</p><p>Swanigan, of the 8800 block of South Normal Avenue in Chicago, was pronounced dead at the scene, according to Illinois state police and the Cook County medical examiner's office. </p><p>Ruiz-Huerta told officers once he knew Swanigan was terrified, he allegedly "put her in danger to get an answer from her" regarding their relationship status. </p>

entries.title: National Trust grant provides preservation hope for modernist East Chicago church
entries.summary: <p>A modernist East Chicago, Indiana, church that mixes architectural Neo-Expressionism with 1970s futurism has been awarded a $150,000 grant from the National Trust for Historic Preservation.</p><p>The funds will help the congregation of St. Mark African Methodist Episcopal Zion Church develop a plan to repair and restore the edifice designed by the late pioneering Black Chicago architect Wendell Campbell, an East Chicago native.</p><p>"This [grant] is really an opportunity for them to step back, create a plan that outlines the existing conditions, create a road map that can really help them reach their goals in terms of preserving this building," said Brandon Bibby, senior preservation architect at the National Trust's African American Cultural Heritage Action Fund.</p><p>And that's an important step toward preserving the 53-year-old building, 4200 Alder St., in Northwest Indiana. The church, still visually arresting, is showing signs of its age.</p><p>St. Mark applied for the grant. The church's officials didn't return calls seeking comment. </p><p>Architect Kurt Garner, who helped the congregation get the church listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2023, said he was glad St. Mark got the funds.</p><p>"To have a building designed with that level of sophistication and symbolism is really quite unique," he said. "I'm so happy for the congregation."</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-e20000" name="image-e20000"></a> <picture data-crop="medium"> <source type="image/webp" width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/bd03fa0/2147483647/strip/true/crop/2000x1122+0+105/resize/490x275!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fde%2F89%2F38dd264d4cc8970b698a06c0251d%2Fst-mark-ame-zion-church-kurt-garner.jpeg 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/0e096db/2147483647/strip/true/crop/2000x1122+0+105/resize/980x550!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fde%2F89%2F38dd264d4cc8970b698a06c0251d%2Fst-mark-ame-zion-church-kurt-garner.jpeg 2x" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <source width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/f51f8a7/2147483647/strip/true/crop/2000x1122+0+105/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fde%2F89%2F38dd264d4cc8970b698a06c0251d%2Fst-mark-ame-zion-church-kurt-garner.jpeg" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <img class="Image" alt="Worship space inside St. Mark A.M.E. Zion Church and the building’s exterior were inspired by the shape of praying hands.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Courtesy of Kurt Garner</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>Built in 1973, St. Mark is one of the finest works of Campbell's distinguished 50-year career.</p><p>The church complex includes a fellowship hall, classrooms and offices. But the signature piece is the church's sanctuary: a sharply-done exercise in material and geometry.</p><p>St. Mark's dominant, multifaceted folded plate roof — married to a base of brick, wood and glass — gives the church's exterior a geodesic look. Under that roof is a nicely-turned worship space that is naturally-lit, open and sublime.</p><p>With its bold, rhythmic forms, the church is Neo-Expressionist — a kind of architecture that rejected the glass box modernism Campbell would have studied as an Illinois Institute of Technology architecture student under Mies van der Rohe in the 1950s.</p><p>"My understanding is when [St. Mark's pastor Rev. St. Clair Williams] along with other officers of the church were meeting with Mr. Campbell, Pastor Williams was sitting at his desk with his hands folded," former St. Mark's pastor Rev. George Walker Jr. told the Northwest Indiana history site Regionology. "Wendell Campbell looked at his hands and said 'That's a unique structure there.' So [the design] is actually in the symbol of praying hands."</p><p>Garner said Campbell's roof system was ahead of its time.</p><p>"The panelized roof system is something that didn't take off, I would say, until the 1990s and 2000s," he said.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-c40000" class="Figure-content"><figcaption class="Figure-caption"><p>The late architect Wendell Campbell</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Sun-Times file</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>St. Mark's design also beckons the future — the optimistic tomorrow that was envisioned in the 1970s.</p><p>"It's an absolutely beautiful building," Bibby said. "In terms of a case study on how to preserve this type of structure, I think this is going to be a really interesting project. They've had lots of roofing issues over the years, which is understandable because of the complex geometry, so being a part of helping them understand the complexities of that and honoring the architect's original intent [will be good.]"</p><p>The grant was among five awarded late last month, as part of the National Trust's Conserving Black Modernism Initiative, a 5-year-old $4.65 million grant partnership between the trust's <a class="Link" href="https://savingplaces.org/action-fund" target="_blank" >African American Cultural Heritage Action Fund </a>and the Getty Foundation.</p><p>Bronzeville's streamlined Art Moderne <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/architecture-design/2025/07/25/grant-preservation-bronzeville-landmark-first-church-deliverance" >First Church of Deliverance</a> was a recipient last year.</p><p>"Conserving Black Modernism has helped communities in nearly every region of the U.S. protect the work of Black architects and has helped broaden the very definition of modernist architecture," Joan Weinstein, director of the Getty Foundation, said.</p><p>And what a great way to give some proper shine to Campbell, especially now. His largest project, Gary's <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/architecture-design/2025/09/08/city-gary-genesis-convention-center-wendall-campbell" target="_blank" >Genesis Convention Center</a> from 1981, was green-lit in June for demolition by the Northwest Indiana Regional Development Authority.</p><p>Fortunately, the area is still left with a wealth of his work from clever midcentury houses in Chatham to the 1970s high-rises at 1240 N. Lake Shore and 4170 N. Marine drives, which he designed with one-time partner John Macsai.</p><p>In 1971, Campbell also co-founded the <a class="Link" href="https://www.noma.net/" target="_blank" >National Organization of Minority Architects</a>, a group that has done much to diversify the architecture industry.</p><p>"There is the architectural significance of the church being [designed by] Wendell Campbell being one of the NOMA founders," Bibby said. "We have tried to make it a priority to uplift the NOMA founders and their work and be a part of honoring that legacy."</p>

entries.title: ‘More to learn’ on Benton harassment case before judging Speaker Chris Welch, Gov. JB Pritzker says
entries.summary: <p>Springfield’s latest sexual harassment scandal has revealed “holes in the system,” according to Gov. JB Pritzker — but not necessarily any missteps by Illinois House Speaker Emanuel “Chris” Welch in responding to allegations of misconduct by a now-disgraced ex-state representative.</p><p>At least not yet, Pritzker said Tuesday, asserting “there is more to learn here, I think, before… anybody’s calling for” a change in House leadership. His comments followed <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/springfield/2026/07/31/harry-benton-report-legislative-inspector-general-speaker-chris-welch-sexual-harassment" target="_blank" ><u>a legislative watchdog’s report</u></a> that Welch’s office knew of a complaint against ex-Rep. Harry Benton nearly three years before the one that led to Benton’s resignation.</p><p>“What the report reveals to me is the holes in the system, that it didn't operate the way that I think was intended originally, and that it needs fixing,” Pritzker said at a West Loop news conference after signing legislation aimed at reining in <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/springfield/2026/05/28/auto-home-insurance-reform-illinois-general-assembly-passage" target="_blank" ><u>insurance rates</u></a>.</p><p>“I look forward to the House members, in particular, putting forward fixes and making sure that that is addressed. I'm sure that the speaker will be engaged in that process. I assume he will,” Pritzker said. “But it's important to me that we remember that victims of sexual harassment ought to have a process that is clear and that investigates and holds accountable people who are guilty of perpetrating these acts.”</p><p>The report released Friday by Legislative Inspector General Mike McCuskey established a “pattern and practice of sexual harassment” by Benton, starting with a 2023 complaint from a former staffer in the Plainfield Democrat’s district office alleging a series of inappropriate comments.</p><p>Welch’s then-chief of staff encouraged the woman to consider filing a complaint with the inspector general but took no further action, while the speaker’s political operation went on to pump some $1.4 million into Benton’s reelection campaign.</p><p>Benton was also accused of harassing a legislative district director at a Springfield bar last year, and in January, a lobbyist reported that Benton made lewd comments to her at a River North bar. He denied wrongdoing.</p><p>The latest incident prompted Welch to exile Benton from the House Democratic Caucus, refer the case to McCuskey’s office and ultimately demand Benton’s resignation, which he tendered last month.</p><p>The speaker has held meetings with members over the past week to allay concerns about his handling of Benton complaints, which hearken back to Springfield’s <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/2018/2/20/18329507/velvet-hammer-mike-madigan-getting-nailed-by-more-and-more-fellow-democrats" target="_blank" ><u>persistent culture of sexual harassment</u></a> under former Speaker Michael Madigan.</p><p>Welch has maintained his office “acted responsibly” and is looking at creating a centralized human resources office, while evaluating if there are other potential “gaps in our policies, our laws, or our workplace practices.”</p><p>Pritzker said he “would like to see and know more” about Welch’s response, but wouldn’t articulate the questions he has for the speaker.</p><p>“I’m gonna leave that to the House members,” Pritzker said. “What I want to know is, how are we gonna fix the system? Because it shouldn't be, in my view, months or years before we have employees who work for state representatives or state Senate members who don't know exactly what the procedure is, exactly who to report to and how to get justice.”</p><p>Republicans have called for Welch to step down as speaker, along with Hoffman Estates Democrat Fred Crespo, whom Welch previously booted from their caucus due to a budget dispute.</p><p>Three legislators stood by Welch during an appearance on WGN-TV: state reps. Lisa Davis, D-Chicago; Norma Hernandez, D-Melrose Park; and Nicolle Grasse, D-Arlington Heights.</p><p>Without naming Welch and stopping well short of calling for him to step down, the chair of the House Democratic Women's Caucus, Arlington Heights state Rep. Mary Beth Canty, said in a statement that questions around the case “deserve a complete and transparent explanation from those involved.”</p><p>Canty criticized “a system that too often prioritizes protecting the institution over protecting the people who work within it.” And she was left “disturbed” by McCuskey’s conduct.</p><p>“When one complainant flagged errors in how her account was recorded, she was met with dismissiveness and belittling,” Canty said. “That is precisely the kind of response that discourages people from coming forward, and it is why the office charged with protecting them must be held to the highest standard.”</p>

entries.title: Así luce Grant Park después de que Lollapalooza desmontó los escenarios
entries.summary: <p>Otro Lollapalooza ya pasó, pero Grant Park tiene un largo camino antes de volver a la normalidad. Entre un fin de semana lleno de lluvia (además de las precipitaciones históricas en toda la región de Chicago este verano) y cuatro días en los que más de 100,000 asistentes al festival descendieron en la ciudad, el espacio verde más grande del centro necesita tiempo para descansar y recuperarse.</p><p>Los trabajos de limpieza ya están en marcha, pero podrían tardar más que en años anteriores, según un portavoz del organizador del festival, C3 Presents. Los organizadores cubren los costos de la instalación del pasto y la mano de obra.</p><p>El año pasado, los organizadores gastaron más de $1 millón en limpieza y restauración tras Lollapalooza. Los organizadores dijeron que los costos de este año podrían ser mayores tras las fuertes lluvias del fin de semana.</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a entries.title: Bears coach Ben Johnson now has 3 premium talents at tight end, and his offense is about to get wild
entries.summary: <p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> used to pick up tight ends in bulk, at one point stockpiling 10 of them in the 2020 offseason, and it became yet another punchline about Ryan Pace and Matt Nagy not knowing what they were doing.</p><p>But no one makes jokes about coach <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2025/09/01/the-bears-and-their-fans-needed-a-truth-teller-they-got-one-in-new-coach-ben-johnson" >Ben Johnson</a> and his collection.</p><p>It helps Johnson doesn’t have 10. Even in an offense intent on using three tight ends at once, the Bears have just seven on their 90-man roster. But he and general manager Ryan Poles have diverted substantial resources to the position to gather the multidimensional pieces Johnson needs to make his offense a nightmare for opponents.</p><p>When veteran Cole Kmet was fairly fresh off signing a $50 million contract extension, the Bears surprised everyone by drafting Colston Loveland 10th overall last year.</p><p>Johnson said he’d play them together.</p><p>Then the Bears picked Stanford’s Sam Roush with the 69th overall pick — just outside the second round — this year, but not to replace Kmet.</p><p>Johnson said he’d play all three together.</p><p>It’s very likely he’ll do a lot of that this season, and it’s at the essence of his motto to, “Make the same things look different and different things look the same,” in his play designs. Tight ends can be effective as receivers or run blockers, and using three of them — known as “13 personnel” with one wide receiver and a running back on the field — expands Johnson’s ability to be unpredictable.</p><p>It also keeps him at the forefront of what has been an emerging trend led by Rams virtuoso play caller Sean McVay. He used the most three-tight-end sets last season at 330, and the Bears were fifth at 94.</p><p>Nobody did it more effectively than McVay, whose Rams had the No. 1 offense and went to the NFC Championship Game after knocking the Bears out of the playoffs. They’ve made a similar investment at the position with Colby Parkinson, Tyler Higbee and Terrance Ferguson.</p><p>Johnson hopes to level up now that he is outfitted with premium talent that he mostly selected. Only Kmet predates his arrival, and the Bears bypassed an affordable out in his contract this offseason. There’s no question he’s a Johnson guy.</p><p>Kmet has proven capable at every facet of the position. Loveland’s strength is as a receiver, but has shown to be a strong blocker, too. Roush is thought of as an in-line blocking tight end, but his 49 catches for 545 yards as a senior shouldn’t be ignored.</p><p>The three of them on the field together gives the Bears eight blockers upfront and automatically signals a run play to the defense, which takes the opponent out of nickel coverage and forces it into its base setup with a combined seven linemen and linebackers.</p><p>“When I first got into the NFL 15 years ago, you would [use] two tight ends, two receivers, and most teams would give you base defense,” Johnson said. “Now, more teams than ever are playing nickel ... so if you want to continue to attack base defense, there's just some merit [to playing three tight ends].</p><p>“More teams are installing their nickel packages earlier on in camp because they're in it more often, and so we may want to attack the lesser-used defense if we can. It just gives you flexibility.”</p><p>Johnson’s menu with 13 personnel is too vast and varied to fully explore, which is a big part of why it gives defensive coordinators headaches, but it creates two basic effects:</p><p>• In the running game, it expands the offensive line by three blockers, which widens the area defenders must cover, and because the defense must respect that tight ends are still receiving threats by keeping at least four defensive backs in coverage, it sets up more double-team blocks to open running lanes.</p><p>“It’s less one-on-one, and you really get to hammer the d-line,” right guard Jonah Jackson said with a giant smile.</p><p>• In the passing game, it makes play action all the more lethal because the formation strongly signals it’s a run and gives any of the three tight ends a chance to escape downfield. And when a defensive play caller sends in heavier, run-stopping defenders, the offense can shift the tight ends out wide and get one-on-one matchups against players who aren’t fast enough to cover them.</p><p>Johnson makes all of that exponentially more difficult to decipher with pre-snap motion, sending an already uncertain defense spiraling even deeper into a guessing game.</p><p>“He plays a lot of eye games ... with those motions and tight ends and doing stuff some different ways,” new Bears linebacker Devin Bush said Tuesday after a practice in which the Bears worked through quite a bit of 13 personnel. “It’s pretty intriguing.”</p><p>Intriguing? Johnson’s adversaries might use words like maddening, perplexing, overwhelming. And the scary thing is last season was only the beginning of it, with Johnson still tweaking the roster and players still learning his scheme. It’s only going to become more sophisticated and potent.</p><p></p><bsp-list-loadmore class="PageListH" data-module data-hide-authors="true" data-hide-categories="true" data-hide-dates="true" data-show-loadmore="true" ><a class="AnchorLink" id="list-bc0001" name="list-bc0001"></a><div class="PageList-header" > <div class="PageList-header-title-wrap" > <div class="PageList-header-title"> <a class="" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="{borderColor=#dfdfdf, pageNumber=1, pullQuoteIcon=[{image=null, narrowImage=null, _template=/image/Image.hbs, alt=null}], inverseColors=false, footerBgColor=#000000, bodyFont=font-3, showListNumbers=false, imagePositionHorizontal=null, rteBodyFont=font-3, headerBottomBorderColor=#111010, titleUrl=https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears, subTitle=null, stickyHeader=true, listTitleColor=#000000, tableCellBorderColor=#ccd1d5, count=20790, relatedListFont=font-1, hideAuthors=true, tertiaryTextColor=#6c6c6c, buttonHoverTextColor=#ffffff, tableFont=font-1, pagination=[{body=[Next Page], href=?p=2, _template=/link/Link.hbs, contentId=null, pianoSectionSlug=null, target=null}], carouselAutoPlay=false, promoTitleFont=font-2, _styledTemplate=/page/list/PageListH.hbs, ctaButtonText=[], primaryTextColor=#2a2a2a, buttonTextColor=#ffffff, linkTextColor=#1a1a1a, hideTitles=false, footerLinkColor=#ffffff, items=[{type=Image, timestamp=1785872894000, _styledTemplate=null, imageAlignment=null, isFeatured=false, target=null, primaryMediaType=null, url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/08/04/bears-coach-ben-johnson-now-has-3-premium-talents-at-tight-end-and-his-offense-is-about-to-get-wild, categoryUrl=https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears, description=[{items=[Using Cole Kmet, Colston Loveland and Sam Roush together reflects his motto to, “Make the same things look different and different things look the same,” in his play designs. entries.title: Former CPS exec charged with scamming pandemic relief programs
entries.summary: <p>A former top Chicago Public School official was charged with ripping off two pandemic relief programs, nearly three years after the school system found she had lied about her income in order to receive loans.</p><p>Crystal Cooper, the district’s former chief operating officer, was among at least 14 CPS staffers who quit in 2023 after the district's inspector general uncovered they had <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/2023/9/6/23860469/ppp-payroll-protection-program-cps-will-fletcher-crystal-cooper" target="_blank" >falsified information on applications</a> for federal Paycheck Protection Program loans. </p><p>In May, Cooper was charged with three counts of wire fraud, according to a recently unsealed federal indictment.</p><p>Beginning in June 2020, Cooper applied for two federal loans through the PPP and Economic Injury Disaster Loan programs, according to the indictment. Those programs were intended to help small businesses survive the pandemic, but they were <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/coronavirus/2023/10/13/23915892/covid-relief-loans-ppp-fraud-chicago-city-hall-watchdog" target="_blank" >overrun with fraud</a>.</p><p>Cooper is accused of lying about her income and the revenue she received from a side business that she’d never disclosed to CPS. She ultimately received over $28,000 in loans that she tapped for “her personal use and benefit,” according to the indictment. Like most of the country’s 11.4 million PPP loans, Cooper’s were forgiven, and she didn't have to pay anything back.</p><p>She pleaded not guilty during her first court appearance on July 23, court records show. She was released on a $10,000 bond and is expected in court again on Aug. 27.</p><p>Her attorney, Andrew Erskine, declined to comment.</p><p><i>This is a developing story. Check back for updates.</i></p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/2023/9/6/23860469/ppp-payroll-protection-program-cps-will-fletcher-crystal-cooper" target="_blank" >Chicago Public Schools COO steps down amid PPP fraud finding by inspector general</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/coronavirus/2023/10/13/23915892/covid-relief-loans-ppp-fraud-chicago-city-hall-watchdog" target="_blank" >More than 1,000 COVID-19 relief loans went to city employees — and many look fraudulent, city’s watchdog says</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p>

entries.title: Johnson: 'I'm the stability' Chicago needs after budget director departs
entries.summary: <p>Mayor Brandon Johnson on Tuesday denied the revolving door at City Hall is a scary sign of instability for Chicago, claiming “I’m the stability” and the “visionary” — and that he will find other people to “carry out my vision.”</p><p>The latest high-level departure from Johnson's City Hall is Budget Director Annette Guzman, whom <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/city-hall/2024/10/29/chicago-budget-2025-brandon-johnson" >the mayor once praised</a> as a "bad, Black, shut-your-mouth" administrator.</p><p>Guzman is “stepping away” to care for her ailing mother, resigning from the $201,564-a-year job she has held from the start of Johnson’s administration.</p><p>Guzman’s abrupt departure is raising serious questions about financial instability because of the timing of it, the wave of high-level departures that preceded it and the enormity of the city’s fiscal problems.</p><p>Chicago faces a $90 million mid-year shortfall, a $1 billion budget gap next year and a $36 billion pension crisis that has two of four city employee pension funds hovering dangerously close to insolvency — even after receiving a city loan to avoid selling assets to pay liabilities.</p><p>The city is weeks away for a grueling election year budget season and days away from an all-important investors conference.</p><p>And Guzman’s resignation comes just days after Acting Chief Financial Officer Steven Mahr and Mahr’s top deputy also resigned.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" Matt O’Shea (19th) wondering “Who’s minding the store?” and where Chicagoans can turn for stability.</p><p>On Tuesday, a defiant Johnson answered.</p><p>“They have stability. They have stability in me,” Johnson told reporters at his weekly City Hall news conference.</p><p>“One person does not run the operation around here. It’s a collection. And even after others have transitioned out, it has not stopped us from building the safest, most affordable big city in America.”</p><p>Calling himself the “visionary” Chicago voters elected, Johnson maintained that so long as the “mission and the vision” that he outlined is "executed” by the changing cast that surrounds him, Chicago will “remain stable under my administration and leadership.”</p><p>“Transitions happen all the time in administrations. whether the turnover in his senior leadership team is a sign of “fractured relationships” with the City Council and others at City Hall.</p><p>“Annette Guzman going to take care of her mother is not a fractured relationship,” the mayor said.</p><p>Pointing to his own father, who has been diagnosed with Alzheimer's, Johnson said, “People don’t prepare you for aging parents. They don’t. And to characterize someone making a personal decision and then coming to a conclusion that has no basis — I find that to be reckless and irresponsible.”</p><p>The mayor’s defiant remarks did nothing to appease the renegade budget coalition.</p><p>In a statement, the so-called “Budget Accountability Coalition” said the “continued wave of leadership departures” from Johnson’s City Hall demands "a full accounting of when and how this administration will deliver on a budget proposal that continues to address structural revenues, efficiencies and reforms needed to close an expected $1 billion FY2027 budget gap, avoid a credit downgrade and put Chicago back on solid fiscal footing."</p><p>Johnson struggled to pass his 2025 budget after <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/city-hall/2025/12/20/chicago-budget-veto-brandon-johnson-alternate-head-tax" >the City Council unanimously rejected</a> his surprise proposal for a $300 million property tax increase.</p><p>Last year, a 29-member majority of moderate and conservative Democrats seized control over a budget process long dictated by Chicago mayor in a budget rebellion not seen since the 1980s power struggle known as Council Wars that saw 29 mostly white alderpersons led by then Alds. Edward Vrdolyak and Edward Burke thwart Mayor Harold Washington’s every move.</p><p>On Tuesday, Johnson argued political tension is “necessary when you’re fighting for the right causes.”</p><p>“Even if you had permanent budget director, but they were screwing working people — what good does that do? It doesn’t do any good for the people who live here,” he said.</p><p>“I will take upset with a safe and affordable city [over] people being quiet and still and people are being harmed. So what is better? To have a little tension and progress or no tension and chaos? I’ll take the tension … any day.”<br></p>

entries.title: Review: Ariana Grande opens up about 'endless, ongoing public scrutiny’ at United Center kickoff
entries.summary: <p>Ariana Grande probably wishes she could just wave a wand and make the whole public discourse about her disappear. But the renewed focus on her image — especially the last few days — has been quite wicked, and the singer addressed it Monday night at the United Center.</p><p>“Is it OK if we get a little real tonight, is that OK?” the “Into You” singer politely asked four songs into her performance, the first of a three-night run at the stadium to wrap up the North American leg of her Eternal Sunshine Tour.</p><p>Just a day prior, a representative for Grande said that the singer <a class="Link" href="https://people.com/ariana-grande-taking-step-back-after-tour-amid-public-health-scrutiny-rep-exclusive-12032395" target="_blank" ><u>would take “a step back from visibility” </u></a>beginning in September, including canceling a previously confirmed role in the West End revival of “Sunday in the Park with George.” As the rep noted in the statement widely picked up by media, the break comes amid “endless, ongoing public scrutiny” about Grande’s appearance, which picked up renewed concern over the weekend.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" The singer announced this week she is stepping back from the public eye when her tour ends.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Katia Temkin</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>On Friday, the 33-year-old star released her latest music video for the title track of her brand-new album, “Petal,” ironically centered on a storyline of brutally attacking her critics. But as the visible bones of Grande’s shoulder and chest are seen in frame after frame, it has sparked questions about her health and well-being.</p><p>Grande wanted to “clear the air” about the topic. Her goal, she said, was “so you know what I’m feeling and not let the world decide and project.” Reading a prepared speech on her phone, Grande clarified that the announcement made by her team on Sunday “was not a reactive or impulsive thing.” As she shared with the sold-out room, “It is something that I had decided to plan that I had quietly made a long time ago, and it’s a decision that was made from a thoughtful and empowered place.</p><p>“I just want to be very, very clear,” she added, appearing nervous but keeping her composure. “Multiple things can be true at the same time. Yes — boundaries — they need to be set. Human beings can need a break sometimes. And also, this can be and will continue to be the greatest experience of my professional and creative life. … No matter what noises exist out there, nothing will ever be able to distort my reality or be more real to me. … The rest of that s--- is not mine to carry, so I don’t carry it. I needed to get out here and differentiate that from my truth for you all.”</p><p>Naturally, Grande was met with supportive cheers from the crowd and passionate screams of “f--- the haters.” Her mother was in attendance at the UC, too, and was seen applauding the speech from the sound booth. class="Figure-credit"><p>Katia Temkin</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>Grande’s fans are incredibly exuberant — many came dressed as her “Wicked” character Glinda or pulled out the black bunny ears from her “Dangerous Woman” era to wear to the show. They counted down the 10 seconds on the preshow timer as if it were New Year’s Eve and about lost it when she brought up “Ricky” in “Thank U, Next” (referencing her alleged on-again flame, Ricky Alvarez). Most also already knew the word-for-word lyrics of the four songs from “Petal” she whipped out toward the end of the show.</p><p>While the Eternal Sunshine Tour is her first in six years, it also comes after a grueling work schedule that included no less than three massive Hollywood movies, three albums, countless collaborations, award show appearances, launching a cosmetic line and appearing as a judge on “The Voice.” Over the weekend, there were rumors she was going to pop up at Lollapalooza.</p><p>Her Eternal Sunshine production would’ve made a better headlining slot at the festival than some of the other performers last weekend. The 26-song set list is packed full of Grande’s strongest work, from “7 Rings” to “One Last Time” and her Gaga collab “Rain on Me,” delivered at their best with a live band. Her voice has never sounded more fortified, with her unreal Mariah Carey-level belting and perfect pitch. She looked stunning in her costume changes, designed by Chicago native Law Roach.</p><p>The show is also a gorgeous, cinematic affair that offers mini-movie interludes between acts that pull from “Alice in Wonderland” and “The Wizard of Oz” with a storyboard that hinted at Grande leaving behind past lives and entering a new era. By the end of the concert, everyone held their breath as Grande walked over to the circular B stage and appeared to ascend into a bright orb in the rafters. It was a stunning moment signifying there’s a rebirth for Grande ahead — and we can only hope that after this much-needed break, she comes back stronger than ever.<br><b></b><br><i>Ariana Grande returns to United Center Wednesday and Thursday.</i></p><h3>Ariana Grande set list Aug. 3, 2026, at United Center</h3><p>"Yes, And?"<br>"Positions"<br>"Dandelion"<br>"The Boy Is Mine"<br>"Eternal Sunshine"<br>"Just Like Magic"<br>"Thank U, Next"<br>"7 Rings"<br>"Imperfect For You"<br>"Warm"<br>"Safety Net"<br>"One Last Time"<br>"Rain On Me (song with Lady Gaga)"<br>"Break Free"<br>"Twilight Zone"<br>"Past Life"<br>"Dangerous Woman"<br>"Honeymoon Avenue"<br>"Hampstead"<br>"Into You"<br>"Hate That I Made You Love Me"<br>"Petal"<br>"Big Feelings"<br>"Never Get Over Me"<br>"We Can’t Be Friends (Wait For Your Love)"<br>"Supernatural"</p>

entries.title: Drew Williams, a Lane football player who was catastrophically injured during a game, dies at 30
entries.summary: <p>Drew Williams, a star athlete at Lane who was paralyzed after suffering a catastrophic brain injury during a game in 2013, died on July 22. He was 30.</p><p>Williams was a standout football and baseball player at Lane and a popular figure around the massive campus at Addison and Western.</p><p>"He had this 'cat that swallowed the canary' smile," said Fred Proesel, who was Lane's head coach when Williams was playing. "He was a leader without seeking to be a leader just because of his personality."</p><p>Jack McLaughlin, a year older than Williams, was Lane's quarterback when the latter was a junior,</p><p>"He was extremely sure of himself at the time and it was infectious," McLaughlin said. "It made you want to be around him. Anyone he ever met he was instantly friends with."</p><p>Williams' playful nature showed up in one of his off-field activities.</p><p>"He had this hobby of collecting school IDs," former teammate Joe Loch said. "He'd collect them like Pokemon cards. He'd try to get the popular senior ones."</p><p>"I'm pretty sure he stole mine at one point," another former teammate, Tony Abreu, said with a laugh.</p><p>Danny Carlson, another football teammate, met Williams when they played youth football together.</p><p>"He's literally been the best athlete I've ever seen," Carlson said. "Drew was a freak show. Drew was always a better athlete than I was, a better friend than I was, a better person than I was."</p><p>Williams was recognized as one of the best players in the city when Lane played Dunbar on Oct. 14. 2013. During the game he collapsed on the field. He was diagnosed with a subdural hematoma and had emergency brain surgery.</p><p>After spending time at Advocate Christ Medical Center, Lurie Children's Hospital and the Rehabilitation Institute of Chicago, Williams was able to return home in May 2014.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" entries.title: Reviewing the summer's breakout high school basketball players
entries.summary: <p>There is so much to digest following the summer months of high school basketball, time used to heavily evaluate prospects while playing with their high school team in June and on the club basketball circuit in July.</p><p>Here are the players who made their presence felt in some way or fashion and the storylines that followed.</p><p>• You can start the Most Improved Player in the Class of 2027 conversation with Tommy Donahue, the 6-4 wing who averaged 6.8 points a game in helping Deerfield to a state runner-up finish last March. Donahue, a proven, space-the-floor shooter who shined all summer, will be one of the breakout players this season.</p><p>• Neuqua Valley’s Cole Kelly is an established marquee name in the sport. He’s already a two-time Sun-Times All-Area selection, boasts high-major offers and has scored over 1,200 points all before his junior year.</p><p>But digging a little deeper, there might not be a bigger stat-sheet-stuffing star in the state. While playing on the Adidas circuit this past offseason with Breakaway, the 6-6 Kelly averaged 16 points, seven rebounds and 5.2 assists in 18 games. In a win over Mike Brown Junior Elite, Kelly went for a triple-double with 20 points, 15 rebounds and 10 assists.</p><p>• Grant Smith of Lyons is a player in the Class of 2028 who will continue to be talked about more and more. The athletic 6-6 junior caught the eye of college coaches this summer.</p><p>• There are a bevy of players with college potential up and down the St. Laurence roster, including recent Central Michigan commit Markese Peoples. But 6-5 rising junior Logan Brown is ascending quickly and is arguably the best prospect in the program. He offers size on the perimeter, his scoring range has improved steadily and he competes at a very high level.</p><p>• We will learn a lot more about plenty of players in the incoming freshman class over the next year, but the first impressions left by Joliet West’s Chad Carter and Bloom’s Larry Ellis were impressive. They will be a dynamic young pair to watch in the upcoming 2026-27 season.</p><p>• DePaul Prep will once again be very good as roles expand and production is added from one very improved player: Blake Choice. Already a defensive stalwart, the 6-3 guard’s versatility now expands to the offensive end of the floor after averaging just 5.4 points a game last season as a junior.</p><p>• Orlando Bohlen, a shooting guard with a scorer’s acumen and who effortlessly buries threes for such a young player, has so far toiled in obscurity. The Public League secret buried at Payton is about to change that. The fun-to-watch Bohlen, who has grown to 6-2, put together a heck of a summer and is among the top sophomores in the state.</p><p>• The Mount Carmel tandem of Ronald Johnson and DK Heard receive the fanfare as players at or near the top of the Class of 2029, but don’t forget about Logan Wessell, an effective and versatile perimeter threat at 6-4 who is poised for a breakout senior season.</p><p>• As a productive big man at 6-7 with skill, the impact of Wheaton Academy’s Hayden Schroeder continues to be felt. Schroeder took a recent visit to Elon and now has offers and interest from the likes of Toledo, Penn, Buffalo, Illinois State, Yale, Valparaiso and Northern Illinois.</p><p>• While Lockport twin brothers Nedas and Nojus Venckus recently received a Division II offer from Winona State, there should be more recruiting traction at that level for the 6-2 guards.</p><p>• With a ton of experience back from a 27-win season, Evanston will be a top five team when the season opens in November. The catalyst, though, will be Ben Ojala. The 6-1 guard not only makes tough shots as a scoring combo guard, but he plays with an edge, and provides a toughness that can flood into a team.</p><p>• Best player and prospect in the state: Bolingbrook rising junior Brady Pettigrew. The 6-3 guard will be the hottest thing in Illinois on the recruiting trail.</p><p>• A rising player in the junior class is Kayden Turner of Peoria High. The 6-4 guard led the Illinois Wolves 16U team in scoring and knocked down 42 three-pointers in 17 games. With Turner and Nigel Moore, a small but dynamic point guard, the Peoria Lions are a team to watch in Class 3A over the next two seasons.</p><p>• He came into high school with some attention and battled some injuries early in his career, but the strides Lincoln Park’s Alvin Robinson continues to show are noticeable. This upcoming season could be the year the 6-3 rising junior elevates his game.</p><p>• Although he plays outside the Chicago area, Moline’s Brady Welch deserves a mention. He is a point guard who truly understands the position he plays. While he can scoot by defenders with quick feet and has range beyond the three-point line, the point guard acumen is what you appreciate when watching the 5-11 rising senior.</p><p>• Oswego has a proven and bona fide scorer in Ethan Vahl, a guard who surpassed 1,000 career points during his freshman and sophomore seasons. Vahl remains one of the top players in the Class of 2028. But the continued improvement of another junior, 6-10 Cole Jansons, is what can push the Panthers to another level. While still an infant in his basketball development, the strides and potential Jansons showed this summer led to offers from SEMO and Northern Illinois.</p><p>• Pound for pound there won’t be many players who impact the upcoming high school basketball season more than Glenbrook North’s 5-9 Nate Fridman. The floor general with elite academics will be a Division III dream for some school and coaching staff.</p>

entries.title: 10 arrested at muddy Lollapalooza, including a backstage brawler, drone operator and poncho seller
entries.summary: <p>At least 10 people were arrested in and around this year’s muddy Lollapalooza music festival in Grant Park, with some facing charges for selling rain ponchos without a permit, illegally flying a drone and punching a backstage security guard with a pocketful of drugs. </p><p>This year’s arrests were split evenly across Thursday, Friday and Saturday, with no arrests Sunday. Last year, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2025/08/04/lollapalooza-chicago-crime-arrest-grant-park-hospital" target="_blank" >12 people were arrested</a> throughout the festival's four days.</p><p>On Thursday night, a 30-year-old Chicago man was arrested for flying an unauthorized drone over Lollapalooza, according to an arrest report.</p><p>When officers found the man operating the drone from the Museum Campus, he gave a false name, refused to cooperate and demanded medical attention, according to Cook County court records. He faces a misdemeanor charge for operating an unauthorized aircraft.</p><p>A 21-year-old Michigan man was arrested Friday after allegedly slapping a woman and then attempting to strike another man, according to his arrest report. He was charged with misdemeanor counts of assault and battery.</p><p>On Saturday, officers arrested a 26-year-old Wheeling man selling $5 rain ponchos outside the festival without a peddler’s license, a police report shows.</p><p>When officers ran his name, they discovered he had a warrant for failing to appear on a drug charge in DuPage County, according to court records. He was issued a citation for illegal peddling. </p><p>The most serious arrest came that same day, when a 23-year-old Wisconsin man was taken into custody after trying to break into a backstage area and punching the security guard who stopped him, according to an arrest report. When Chicago police searched the man, they found a bag of suspected cocaine in his wallet. </p><p>He was charged with a felony count of possession and misdemeanors for battery and trespassing. He’s the only person facing a felony charge from the weekend. </p><p>The six others arrested during the festival were hit with misdemeanor charges, including trespassing, battery and reckless conduct. Those charged ranged in age from 18 to 39.</p><p>As arrests fell, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/lollapalooza/2026/08/03/hospitalizations-arrests-lollapalooza-grant-park-oemc" target="_blank" >hospitalizations rose</a> this year, with 67 festivalgoers taken for treatment.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/lollapalooza/2026/08/03/hospitalizations-arrests-lollapalooza-grant-park-oemc" target="_blank" >Hospitalizations up, arrests down across 4 days of Lollapalooza</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/lollapalooza/2026/08/03/heres-what-grant-park-looks-like-after-lollapalooza-clears-the-stages" target="_blank" >Here’s what Grant Park looks like after Lollapalooza clears the stages</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/2026/08/01/as-lollapaloozas-original-fans-grow-up-attending-with-their-offspring-feels-well-perfectly-fine" target="_blank" >As Lollapalooza’s original fans grow up, attending with their offspring feels, well, perfectly fine</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p>

entries.title: The cascading effect of Coby Bryant's injury leaves Bears more problems to solve
entries.summary: <p>In an austere offseason, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/08/03/bears-s-coby-bryant-carted-off-from-practice-with-apparent-knee-injury" target="_blank" >Coby Bryant</a> was the splurge.</p><p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> bet big on him, letting all-pro safety Kevin Byard and four-year starter Jaquan Brisker leave this offseason and giving him a three-year, $40 million deal.</p><p></p><p>The safety had been where the Bears want to go — the Super Bowl. He had what Bears defensive coordinator Dennis Allen decided they needed most — speed. And his addition made the Bears more comfortable drafting a first-round safety, Dillon Thieneman, to pair with him.</p><p>It took less than an hour of first day of padded practice Monday for all that to crumble. Bryant hyperextended his left knee, suffering a bone bruise and a small break that will keep him out 8-10 weeks.</p><p>The cascading effect of the injury gives the Bears a problem to solve. Or, rather, many problems.</p><p></p><p>It will take creativity from Allen and flexibility from the players.</p><p></p><p>“I mean I think that's all of our jobs,” Allen said Tuesday. “I think that's the coaches' job, I think that's the players' job. You know nothing ever goes exactly how you planned, right? You have to be able to adjust.”</p><p>Life after Bryant will be nothing new for Allen. He’s entering his second season as the Bears’ defensive coordinator and has still never held a single training camp practice with his starting defensive backs healthy. Cornerback Jaylon Johnson hurt his groin training in the weeks before camp began last year. Nickel cornerback Kyler Gordon, who was out most of last season, began this year’s training camp on the Physically Unable to Perform list with a calf injury.</p><p>Then there’s Thieneman, the rookie whose transition to the NFL was supposed to be eased by the very presence of Bryant. Allen said the Bears won’t “put any higher expectations” on the first-round pick with Bryant gone. His absence, though, risks stunting Thieneman's growth. That's the most alarming possibility among the many consequences of Bryant's injury.</p><p>“We've got Dillon that's gonna have big big shoes to fill,” linebacker Devin Bush said. “Him being a rookie … he’s got to come up to speed.”</p><p>Bryant’s injury is a Gordon problem, too. Bears coaches have been annoyed for months by Gordon’s slow recovery. When he wasn’t healthy enough to start camp, the Bears were forced to play safety Cam Lewis, whom they signed away from the Bills in March, at slot cornerback. Lewis played 145 of his 373 defensive snaps in the slot last year — and the rest at safety. His versatility was his greatest strength. Now Lewis will be penciled into a starting safety position opposite Thieneman.</p><p>That could change, though, if safety Elijah Hicks returns after starting training camp on PUP with shin pain. General manager Ryan Poles expected a quick recovery for Hicks, who started seven games in 2024 when Brisker was concussed. The Bears added depth Tuesday by signing safety Marlen Sewell, who won a brief look from the Chiefs coming out of their tryout camp. For now, at least, the Bears are unlikely to try to trade for help at the position.</p><p>With Lewis at safety, veteran Jaylon Jones, the team’s third-string slot cornerback, played with the starters during Tuesday’s practice. Special teams ace Josh Blackwell can play in the slot, too, but the Bears coaching staff rarely used him last year when injuries ravaged his position. He played just three defensive snaps. Fourth-round pick Malik Muhammad is learning how to play the nickel position but has a long way to go.</p><p>Playing the slot is different than being outside. To react quickly, you need to know where to keep your eyes. That takes practice.</p><p>“If you put your eyes in the right spot,” Allen said, “you have a chance to be right.”</p><p></p><p>And many more chances to be wrong.</p><p></p><bsp-list-loadmore class="PageListH" data-module data-hide-authors="true" data-hide-categories="true" data-hide-dates="true" data-show-loadmore="true" ><a class="AnchorLink" id="list-bc0001" name="list-bc0001"></a><div class="PageList-header" > <div class="PageList-header-title-wrap" > <div class="PageList-header-title"> <a class="" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="{borderColor=#dfdfdf, pageNumber=1, inverseColors=false, footerBgColor=#000000, pagination=[{body=[Next Page], href=?p=2, _template=/link/Link.hbs, contentId=null, pianoSectionSlug=null, target=null}], bodyFont=font-3, showListNumbers=false, imagePositionHorizontal=null, rteBodyFont=font-3, headerBottomBorderColor=#111010, titleUrl=https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears, subTitle=null, stickyHeader=true, listTitleColor=#000000, tableCellBorderColor=#ccd1d5, count=20790, relatedListFont=font-1, hideAuthors=true, tertiaryTextColor=#6c6c6c, buttonHoverTextColor=#ffffff, tableFont=font-1, carouselAutoPlay=false, promoTitleFont=font-2, _styledTemplate=/page/list/PageListH.hbs, ctaButtonText=[], primaryTextColor=#2a2a2a, buttonTextColor=#ffffff, linkTextColor=#1a1a1a, hideTitles=false, footerLinkColor=#ffffff, items=[{description=[{items=[Using Cole Kmet, Colston Loveland and Sam Roush together reflects his motto to, “Make the same things look different and different things look the same,” in his play designs. entries.title: Jed Hoyer added needed pitching at trade deadline, now Craig Counsell, Cubs must put puzzle pieces together
entries.summary: <p>Suddenly, things are mighty crowded on the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" >Cubs</a>’ pitching staff.</p><p>Earlier in the summer, injuries stretched the team’s pitching depth to its limits. But after <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/03/cubs-mlb-trade-deadline-jed-hoyer-top-prospects-trades-kevin-gausman-clay-holmes-ryan-zeferjahn-braxton-garrett-tyrone-taylor" >Jed Hoyer’s aggressive trade deadline</a> Monday, there are new questions on the North Side, chiefly:</p><p>How are the Cubs going to fit all their new pitching puzzle pieces together?</p><p>Questions, maybe. But not problematic ones, so says the skipper.</p><p>“You might look at it and say, ‘Oh, we’ve got too many starters. What are we going to do?’ We’ll figure it out,” manager Craig Counsell said Monday. “And if that’s a problem? I don’t consider it a problem. We’re going to have to find some different ways and be creative, but we’ll do that.”</p><p>Indeed, having too many pitchers to choose from strikes as the proverbial good problem to have.</p><p>But the Cubs do have a puzzle to put together over the regular season’s final two months to best position themselves for the deep October run they’re dreaming of.</p><p>The headline additions at the trade deadline, righty starters <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/02/dodgers-getting-tarik-skubal-only-makes-cubs-road-tougher" >Kevin Gausman</a> and <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/03/cubs-trade-deadline-clay-holmes-mets" >Clay Holmes</a> — who will make their Cubs debuts this weekend against the Royals — are easy to slot into the rotation alongside lefties Matthew Boyd and Shota Imanaga, who have turned in <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/07/30/cubs-mlb-trade-deadline-pitching-starting-rotation-matthew-boyd-shota-imanaga-colin-rea-david-peterson-javier-assad-tarik-skubal" >one ace-like performance after another of late</a>.</p><p>Holmes, who has made three recent rehab starts in his journey back from a fractured fibula, has experience as an All-Star closer from his time with the Yankees, during which he pitched in the World Series. He’s a starter now, but might the entirely different world of postseason pitching strategy see him return to a relief role?</p><p>“You want to do whatever you can to win a ballgame at that point,” he said. “That’s what makes the playoffs so fun. It’s really not about one person, it’s not about a role. It’s about, ‘What do you have to give? And what can you do for the team to win?’</p><p>“Whatever it is down the stretch, whether they need a starter, the bullpen, I just love being out there when big outs are needed. Whenever that is, I’m all for it.”</p><p>Beyond the aforementioned quartet, there’s lefty David Peterson, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/07/28/cubs-david-peterson-mlb-trade-deadline-mets-jed-hoyer-pitching-staff-rotation-craig-counsell-ground-ball-rate" >who has been quite effective</a> since coming over in a trade earlier this summer. Things figure to get interesting when righty Edward Cabrera comes back from the injured list in the coming weeks.</p><p>Is a six-man rotation brewing on the North Side?</p><p>“I think we will go with six at certain times, yes,” Counsell said. “Every time through? No, we can’t do that. It puts too much on the bullpen.”</p><p>Righty Colin Rea, who in fill-in duty has made more starts (19) than anyone on the team besides Imanaga, will join the relief corps, at least in the short term.</p><p>“He’s going to skip a turn here, he’s going to be in the bullpen for the next turn [through the rotation],” Counsell said. “Past that, I don’t know what’s going to happen, and we’ll go from there. … My guess is that Colin will make more starts for this team this year, because we’re going to need it.”</p><p>Right-hander Javier Assad started Tuesday opposite Tarik Skubal and has performed well as an injury fill-in. Along with Rea, he figures to soon become the starting depth the team struggled with during last year’s postseason, as does lefty Braxton Garrett, at Triple-A Iowa after arriving in a deadline deal.</p><p>Though Hoyer made splashy additions with Gausman and Holmes, pitching depth was truly at the top of his wishlist. Mission accomplished on that front, as the Cubs learned earlier this summer you can’t have too much pitching.</p><p>“We’re more talented than we were 48 hours ago,” Hoyer said Monday. “Providing more talent and more depth was something that was critical. … We’ve spent the entire season making outside additions, small [ones], trying to get through the season.</p><p>“Given how the season’s gone, given how we’ve had to consistently make those sort of moves over and over, really reinforcing our pitching staff for these last 50 games made a lot of sense.”</p><p></p><p></p><bsp-listcarousel entries.title: Dumpsters full of books showed up outside former Acero schools. Parents and teachers worked to salvage them
entries.summary: <p>Sarah Parchem gasped when she came across a Facebook post on Sunday showing a dumpster full of books and school supplies outside of Fuentes Elementary School in Avondale.</p><p>As the mother of a rising kindergartner who values reading, Parchem said the photo almost made her cry. But she also saw an opportunity. Parchem hopped in her car and spent two hours dumpster diving that morning looking for anything she could salvage.</p><p>She wasn't alone. For days, parents, teachers and community members searched through the dumpster outside of Fuentes for anything of use. A similarly stocked dumpster was seen outside of Santiago Elementary School in the Ukrainian Village neighborhood.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item"
